reasoning_trace: The gecko gripper embodiment requires clean, dry, smooth, flat, and parallel surfaces for optimal dry adhesion. The query object image shows a hand-molded, uneven, painted pot with curved, non-flat sidewalls and a rough texture. This is highly incompatible with effective gecko pad engagement. Although the gecko gripper can technically still grasp objects via limited frictional support when adhesion fails, a significantly higher normal force is required to compensate for the lack of adhesion and irregular geometry. Given the maximum limit of 8 N and an estimated lightweight object, a conservative high-end normal force of 5.5 N is chosen to ensure secure frictional grasping under unfavorable contact conditions.
